page: OVHcloud r3-32 is a memory-optimized virtual server hosted on the KVM hypervisor. It features 4 dedicated physical cores powered by an AMD EPYC processor running at 2.3 GHz, utilizing the x86_64 architecture with one thread per core. The hardware configuration includes 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding 8.0 GB of RAM per core, alongside a local 100 GB NVMe SSD for storage. Network connectivity is provisioned with a baseline bandwidth of 1 Gbps, and the server includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong single-core capabilities, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance and Geekbench text processing scoring in the top 25%. Multi-core CPU performance, memory bandwidth, and Redis SET operations fall into the average tier. However, the server exhibits weaker performance in static web serving throughput, which registers at 4.42 GB/sec, and medium-model LLM prompt processing, placing those metrics in the bottom 25%.

From a resource density perspective, the dedicated AMD EPYC cores without hyperthreading offer predictable compute performance, making this instance a cost-efficient option for memory-intensive workloads that do not require massive parallel processing. The primary tradeoffs include the modest 1 Gbps network baseline and lower throughput for static web serving. This server is best suited for memory-bound applications, database operations, caching layers, and text processing tasks.
